You are going to evaluate a research idea on five criteria: Novelty, Feasibility, Clarity, Impact and Validity.

As part of your evaluation, you can refer to the research problem, the target paper, and the closest prior work found by a literature search for this idea.
Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.
Target paper title: Adapting Visual-Language Models for Generalizable Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
Target paper abstract: Recent advancements in large-scale visual-language pre-trained models have led to significant progress in zero/few-shot anomaly detection within natural image domains. However, the substantial domain divergence between natural and medical images limits the effectiveness of these methodologies in medical anomaly detection. This paper introduces a novel lightweight multi-level adaptation and comparison framework to repurpose the CLIP model for medical anomaly detection. Our approach integrates multiple residual adapters into the pre-trained visual encoder, enabling a stepwise enhancement of visual features across different levels. This multi-level adaptation is guided by multi-level, pixel-wise visual-language feature alignment loss functions, which recalibrate the model's focus from object semantics in natural imagery to anomaly identification in medical images. The adapted features exhibit improved generalization across various medical data types, even in zero-shot scenarios where the model encounters unseen medical modalities and anatomical regions during training. Our experiments on medical anomaly detection benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly surpasses current state-of-the-art models, with an average AUC improvement of 6.24% and 7.33% for anomaly classification, 2.03% and 2.37% for anomaly segmentation, under the zero-shot and few-shot settings, respectively. Source code is available at: https://github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD

The research idea:
TITLE: Similarity-weighted conformal thresholds on residual-CDF scores
SUMMARY: Keep residual-CDF scoring but replace the plain split-conformal quantile with a weighted conformal quantile in which supports similar to the test image (CLIP CLS similarity) count more, so the threshold adapts to each image while keeping an approximate false-positive bound under covariate shift.
HYPOTHESIS: Similarity-weighted conformal thresholds reduce the spread of realised false-positive rates across held-out datasets by at least 5 points relative to unweighted conformal thresholds at K >= 8, while keeping the mean realised false-positive rate within 2 points of alpha.
RATIONALE: The parent's split-conformal step assumes that test normals are exchangeable with the supports; across BMAD datasets this fails when a test image comes from a different part of the anatomy or another scanner than most supports. Weighted conformal prediction (Tibshirani et al., 2019) keeps an approximate guarantee under covariate shift by weighting calibration points with a likelihood ratio, which can be approximated by similarity of global features. The substitute targets the same quantity (a per-image threshold with controlled false positives) with the same evaluation.
METHOD: 1) Residual-CDF scoring as in the parent (exact LOO). 2) For test image x: weights w_i = exp(cos(cls_x, cls_i)/tau) over supports, plus w_{K+1} for the test point; tau from source validation. 3) Threshold = weighted (1 - alpha) quantile of support LOO image scores with the test point's mass at +infinity. 4) Report realised FPR and sensitivity at alpha in {0.1, 0.2}. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: unweighted conformal thresholds. Metrics: realised FPR per dataset and its spread, sensitivity. Falsified if the spread of realised FPR is not reduced.
